claim_being_audited: That certifying the model for launch is policy-compliant and evidentially supportable despite the student-aid-advising segment missing target, because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and the remaining gap can be handled through documented limitations and ongoing monitoring.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the certification satisfied the release policy for this material limitation.
Treat the weakness as material because it affects a named launch use case and is named in customer commitments; non-core or low-volume framing does not negate materiality.
Require evidence of one of the policy-safe paths before launch: resolution of the limitation, required disclosure, or approved risk acceptance.
Treat public AI governance guidance as contextual support only, not as a substitute for internal policy compliance evidence.
Where a required support link remains unresolved but some facts favor the actor, classify as suspicious rather than compliant.
evidence_requests: Evidence that the student-aid-advising gap was disclosed in the model card or other required launch materials before certification.
Evidence of an approved risk acceptance covering this material limitation before launch.
Evidence that the named pilot commitments were amended, excluded, or otherwise no longer make this a named launch use case.
The outcome of the open legal review on whether disclosure is required.
Any internal approval record expressly authorizing certification despite the unresolved segment gap.
specific_concerns: The available record shows the affected segment is a named launch use case and is named in two university pilot commitments, which makes the weakness material under the stated policy.
The actor summary says legal review on disclosure remains open, leaving a required policy predicate unresolved.

The cited policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch; the summary provides no evidence that either condition has been met.
Aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support general launch readiness but do not by themselves resolve materiality or disclosure obligations for the failing segment.
Public governance guidance about documenting limitations and monitoring risk is supportive context, not evidence that the specific internal release-policy requirement was satisfied.
unsupported_claims: That certification is compliant on the current record without evidence of disclosure completion, issue resolution, or approved risk acceptance.
That documented limitation handling and post-launch monitoring are sufficient substitutes for the policy's explicit pre-launch disclosure or approved-risk-acceptance requirement.
Any implication that aggregate launch readiness alone overcomes materiality for the named student-aid-advising use case.
